title: Set x-session-affinity so prefix caching actually hits
description:
THE LARGEST COST LEVER FOUND. The runaway run spent $49.80 on 46,098,950 input tokens against only 1,019,075 output tokens — 98% of the spend was re-sending context — and NOT ONE of its 892 calls hit a cache.

Measured, not inferred:
  gateway cache_ttl = 0, and cached = false on all 892 calls
  the model's own response reports prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens = 0 on a 71,759-token prompt
  the request prefix IS byte-identical across calls (verified on two requests hours apart: same system prompt, same opening bytes)

So the prefix is cacheable and nothing is caching it.

Per Cloudflare's docs (developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/features/prompt-caching/): Workers AI enables PREFIX CACHING BY DEFAULT for select models, cached input tokens bill at a discount, and the response surfaces cached counts in usage. Critically: "Use the x-session-affinity header with a unique session identifier to maximize cache hit rates by routing requests to the same model instance", and "a single token difference invalidates the cache from that point onward".

THE FIX: cloud/factory/src/gateway.ts builds the upstream headers (it already sets cf-aig-metadata and cf-aig-authorization) and does NOT set x-session-affinity. Without it, a run's calls scatter across model instances, each with its own prefix cache, so the hit rate is ~0 no matter how stable the prefix is. Set x-session-affinity to the run id — it is exactly the "unique session identifier" the doc asks for, it is already on the token row, and it keeps a run's traffic on one instance.

Note the two caches are different things and only one of them matters here. The GATEWAY response cache (cache_ttl) matches identical requests to identical responses and is near-useless for an agentic loop, because every turn's request differs. PREFIX caching is the one that pays, because the loop's prompt grows by appending while its first ~60k tokens stay fixed.

VERIFY BY MEASUREMENT, not by reading the header back: run the same epic twice and compare cached_tokens and cost per call. A run whose prefix is 60k of 70k tokens should show most of its input billed at the cached rate.

Also worth checking while there: whether anything the factory injects early in the message array varies per call (a run id, a timestamp, a wall-clock note). A single differing token near the start invalidates everything after it, and that would defeat affinity even once the header is set.

acceptance_criteria: A cloud run reports non-zero cached_tokens on calls after the first, and cost per call falls measurably against a baseline run; the affinity identifier is the run id; a documented check confirms no per-call variation exists early in the message array.
